_readme: Every entry must carry a `reason`, and a `ticket` where one exists: an entry
without a reason is a parse FAILURE, because the whole value of this list is
that somebody had to say why. Keys are exact `Class.verb` names - there is no
wildcard and no module-level suppression, so a verb that is not named here and
An entry whose verb has since found a caller is reported STALE, so this list
cannot grow into a description of a different tree than the one it gates.
This is not a backlog of work to do. It records verbs whose zero-caller state
is CORRECT because the moment that would call them does not ship yet, and names
the decision that is waiting on it.

EventApi.resolve.reason: DEF-0315. The only caller of NationApi.resolve_conflict, so the declared war_of_the_nine_fords standoff can never be settled and the river march never changes hands. ADR 0085 forbids making the political layer decide the winner, so no call site may be invented: no shipped moment produces a verdict.

EventApi.catalog.reason: BL-0907. The authored event definitions are read inside the module through `_catalog()` and reach a player through `available`/`summary`. `catalog()` is the raw authored table; it has no separate consumer, and `EventApi.events` - which DOES need one - is reported rather than exempted.

EventApi.active.reason: BL-0907. The in-flight event rows are folded into `EventApi.summary`, which a screen calls, so the read model ships through the verb that has a caller. `active()` is the unfiltered form of a summary key.
